claims.statement: Deep Agents is a three-layer stack: LangGraph is the runtime (state, checkpoints, streaming, interrupts), LangChain create_agent is the agent abstraction that builds the model-plus-tools-plus-middleware loop on top of LangGraph, and Deep Agents is an opinionated harness on top of create_agent.
Deep Agents does not introduce a new runtime; create_deep_agent() assembles the default middleware stack and configures backends, subagents, skills, memory, and profiles on top of create_agent().

The dependency direction runs Deep Agents to LangChain create_agent to LangGraph, so each layer depends on the one below it and any LangGraph CompiledStateGraph can be passed in as a Deep Agents sub-agent.

LangGraph owns durable execution behavior — graph state carried between steps, checkpoints, streaming, and interrupt-based pause/resume — while LangChain create_agent owns the model/tool/repeat loop shape.

Deep Agents extends LangChain's AgentState with DeepAgentState, whose messages field uses a DeltaChannel reducer so checkpoint growth stays linear (O(N)) rather than quadratic (O(N^2)) on long threads.

create_deep_agent() is the assembly point that resolves the model and harness profile, resolves the backend, conditionally builds the default general-purpose subagent, composes the final system prompt, and delegates to LangChain's create_agent(...) to produce the runnable graph.

After building the graph, create_deep_agent() calls .with_config(...) to attach Deep Agents metadata (ls_integration, lc_versions, lc_agent_name) and a recursion_limit of 9,999 so long multi-step runs are not cut off.
When a tool is missing the cause is middleware assembly or profile tool exclusions, whereas when a tool is visible but fails the cause is backend capability or filesystem permission enforcement.

The main-agent middleware stack is assembled in graph.py with optional skills, filesystem, subagent, summarization, patch-tool-calls, optional asynchronous subagent, profile, prompt-caching, memory, tool-exclusion, and human-in-the-loop middleware; subagents get their own middleware stacks.
The repository is a monorepo under libs/ with each package independently versioned, where deepagents is the core SDK exposing create_deep_agent, middleware, and pluggable backends.
The code package is Deep Agents Code, a pre-built terminal coding agent built on the SDK, run via the dcode command with a TUI, remote sandboxes, memory, skills, and headless mode.
The acp package provides Agent Client Protocol integration for running a Deep Agent inside editors like Zed, including exposing dcode as an ACP server.
The evals package is the evaluation suite with Harbor integration for benchmarking agent behavior.
The talon package is an experimental local runtime host for long-running agents, providing channel adapters and cron schedulers.
The partners package holds provider/sandbox integrations (Daytona, Modal, Runloop, Vercel, QuickJS).

Most Deep Agents-specific code lives in three places under libs/deepagents/deepagents/: middleware/ adds harness behavior to the loop, backends/ decides where files, memory, and shell execution live, and profiles/ tunes the harness per provider or model; graph.py is the construction entrypoint.

create_deep_agent() uses StateBackend when no backend is supplied, composes the caller prompt with the harness profile prompt, and forwards checkpointer, store, context schema, debug, name, cache, and state schema to LangChain create_agent().

Custom Deep Agents state schemas are expected to subclass DeepAgentState to retain its DeltaChannel message reducer; the schema is forwarded to declarative subagents but compiled and remote subagents retain their independently configured schemas.

Profile exclusion validation rejects protected middleware exclusions, private names, ambiguous class matches, and exclusions that match no assembled middleware, preventing silent partial harness configuration.

The package manifests make deepagents-code a dependency consumer of deepagents, deepagents-evals a consumer of both deepagents and deepagents-code, and deepagents-talon a consumer of both deepagents and deepagents-code.
The SDK test configuration excludes benchmark-marked tests by default and promotes unexpected warnings to errors; focused graph tests verify compiled-graph metadata wiring.

Deep Agents Code's create_cli_agent() is the product assembly point: it builds an SDK agent with a composite backend, CLI context schema, CLI middleware, interrupt policy, checkpoint/store, subagents, and a sanitized assistant name; registered extensions replace same-named tools and middleware before construction.

AgentServerACP can support session loading only with a durable LangGraph checkpointer; when enabled, it restores the graph thread, verifies the original working directory, and replays the conversation to the ACP client after restart.

Talon's DeepAgentRuntime constructs its SDK graph at start after resolving subagents and approval configuration; each invoke refreshes dynamic tools, can rebuild for changed approvals, establishes request-scoped contexts and resets them in finally, while stop cancels background work before graph/checkpointer cleanup.

Talon is alpha software without production-grade human approval policy, channel administrator controls, sandbox execution isolation, or multi-tenant boundaries; channel users must therefore be treated as having direct access to the operator's agent, credentials, MCP tools, and local host resources.

The evaluation suite runs agents against real LLMs, captures tool calls, file mutations, and final responses, and scores correctness and efficiency; its Harbor integration runs sandboxed benchmarks such as Terminal Bench 2.0.
The deepagents package publicly exports create_deep_agent, DeepAgentState, common filesystem, memory, rubric, and subagent middleware types, and registration APIs for harness and provider profiles.
deepagents-acp depends on deepagents and Agent Client Protocol, and AgentServerACP accepts either a compiled graph or a factory that builds a graph from ACP session context.
The release manifest records independent versions for deepagents, ACP, Code, Talon, and the Daytona, Modal, Runloop, Vercel, and QuickJS partner packages.
The code package exposes both deepagents-code and dcode console commands through deepagents_code:cli_main.
The Talon package exposes the deepagents-talon command through deepagents_talon.__main__:main.

Talon invokes the graph with the request conversation ID as LangGraph thread_id, retries retryable failures with capped exponential backoff while propagating cancellation, and nudges empty responses before forcing a summary.

Talon captures the graph selected for an invocation in a ContextVar, so replacement graphs apply to later turns while a running invocation retains its original graph; tool and subagent reloads construct a replacement graph before publishing it.
Talon resumes tool-approval interrupts with Command resume payloads and fails an invocation after 50 approval rounds rather than looping indefinitely.
If Talon background workers do not stop during shutdown, stop raises and intentionally retains graph and checkpointer resources rather than closing them beneath active writes.

Talon's default workspace is the current directory, its per-invocation recursion limit defaults to 500 and can be configured with DEEPAGENTS_TALON_RECURSION_LIMIT, and its default persisted host state uses checkpoints.sqlite under the assistant directory.
